text: Annual profections hand each year of your life to a planetary manager, and this year the assignment falls to the Sun. In this old timing technique, every birthday advances a simple count, the count lands on one planet, and that planet becomes lord of the year, coloring the whole twelve months with its agenda. A Sun year is about being seen. Questions of identity, recognition, and direction come forward: who you are, what you stand for, whether the life you are living still looks like you. Expect more moments where you are asked to step up, take the lead, or put your name on something. Attention finds you more easily, which is welcome when you are proud of the work and uncomfortable when you would rather stay in the wings. Authority is a theme too, both the authorities over you and your own. Bosses, mentors, parents, anyone who plays a guiding role can figure in the year's story, and so can your appetite to stop orbiting other people's plans. Vitality matters in a plain physical sense as well: the Sun runs the engine, so how you spend and restore your energy shows results faster than usual. Here is the practical part. Because the Sun holds the office, your own natal Sun is where the story concentrates. Its condition in your birth chart sets the tone of the year, and transits to it act like memos to the manager: when a moving planet crosses or aspects your Sun this year, that week tends to matter more than it normally would. Your solar return, the birthday moment itself, opens the ledger, so it is worth noticing what gathers around it. A Sun year tends to clarify. By its end you usually know better what you want your life to be about, not because one event announced it, but because a year of being asked to show yourself leaves you more visible to yourself as well.

This year has a manager, and it is the Moon. That is how annual profections work: each birthday moves a count forward by one, the count points at a planet, and that planet takes charge of the year as its lord. Under the Moon's management, the year runs on the tides of daily life. The Moon governs the body, the home, the people who raised you and the people you look after, and the moods that rise and fall underneath your plans. So this tends to be a year where those things ask for attention. Home may need tending, changing, or rethinking. Family and the small circle you actually live among take up more room. Care flows in both directions: you may find yourself looking after someone, or finally letting someone look after you. Your body speaks more loudly too, in appetite, sleep, and energy, and it rewards being listened to. Feelings carry real information now rather than background noise. The Moon is the fastest thing in the sky, which gives a lunar year its texture: not one big plot but many small chapters, a rhythm of waxing and waning you can learn to ride. Each month's New and Full Moons land like scheduled check-ins from the year's manager. And since this is the Moon's year, your own natal Moon is the point to keep an eye on. Its condition in your birth chart describes how the year is likely to feel from the inside, and transits to it mark the days and weeks when things actually move. When something in the current sky reaches that point, the tide comes in. You come out of a Moon year knowing your own needs better. Not the needs you think you should have, the ones you actually do, learned the way the Moon teaches everything: by repetition, in waves.

By the count astrologers call annual profections, where every birthday hands the year to a new planetary lord, this is a Mercury year for you. Mercury runs the traffic of life: words, ideas, messages, paperwork, trade, short trips, learning, and the thousand small transactions that keep everything else moving. A year under its management is busy in exactly that way. Expect more conversations that matter, more writing and reading, more forms and logistics than usual. Study goes well now, whether formal or the self-taught kind, and so does anything that lives on skill with language or numbers. Siblings, neighbors, colleagues, the people you exchange words with daily rather than vows, often step forward in the year's story. The year asks you to be precise. Agreements hinge on wording. Misunderstandings cost more than they usually do, and clearing one up pays more too. Your mind is the year's main instrument, so its habits, what you feed it, how you rest it, whether you say what you mean, become practical matters instead of abstractions. The way to follow the plot is to watch Mercury itself. Your natal Mercury's condition describes what kind of manager you got, and the transits it receives this year mark the weeks when the year's business concentrates. Mercury also turns retrograde several times a year, and in a Mercury year those stretches are not generic annoyances but scheduled reviews of your own agenda: drafts come back, plans get revised, old conversations reopen on purpose. Treat them as part of the curriculum. A Mercury year rarely delivers one grand event. It delivers information. By the end you have usually learned something you could not have planned to learn, met people through words alone, and heard your own thinking clearly enough to change it.

The lord of your year, by the birthday count called annual profections, is Venus. One planet takes management of each year of your life, and a Venus administration has a recognizable style: it works through attraction rather than force. This tends to be a year where relationships move toward the center. New connections form more easily, existing ones ask to be enjoyed rather than merely maintained, and old ruptures become easier to repair, since Venus is the planet of treaties as much as of romance. Pleasure is on the agenda too, and it is not a distraction from the year's work; it is the year's work. What you find beautiful, what you actually enjoy, what makes life feel worth the trouble: a Venus year raises those questions and takes the answers seriously. Taste sharpens. You may care more about your surroundings, your appearance, the look and feel of what you make. Money enters through the same door, since Venus concerns value: what you will pay for, what you charge, what you think your own effort is worth. The center of gravity is your natal Venus. Its condition in your chart tells you how smoothly the year's charm is likely to run, and the transits that reach it are the moments when themes turn into events: a meeting, an invitation, an offer, a reconciliation. Those weeks carry the year's main appointments, so they are worth watching for. The risk of a Venus year is drift, pleasant days that add up to nothing chosen. The gift is the opposite, and it is real: a year that teaches you what you love by letting you have some of it. You tend to leave with better company than you entered with, and a clearer sense of what deserves a place in your life because it delights you.

Each birthday, by the old technique of annual profections, appoints one planet to run the coming year, and this time the office goes to Mars. Mars manages through heat. A year under it favors effort, courage, competition, and the kind of progress that only happens when someone finally pushes. Things you have circled for a long time can get done now, because the year keeps handing you the nerve to act. The same heat has edges. Conflict comes more easily: disputes surface, tempers shorten, and situations that were quietly unfair stop being tolerable. That is not a malfunction. Part of what a Mars year does is show you where your anger has been living and what it has been trying to protect. Physical life turns up in the story too. Mars rules exertion, and the year tends to go better when your body has real work to do; unspent drive is what turns into friction. Cutting is a Mars verb, and some of the year's best moves are subtractions: ending what is finished, saying the no you have owed someone, separating from what dulls you. Watch your own Mars to see how the year will fight. Its natal condition describes the temperament of the manager you have been assigned, and transits to your Mars this year mark the flashpoints, the weeks when the contests and the breakthroughs cluster. Mars in the current sky deserves attention during its own year as well; when it stations or crosses a sensitive point of your chart, the volume rises. To be clear, a Mars year is not a sentence to strife. Plenty of them are remembered as the year the training habit stuck, the venture launched, the hard boundary held. What it will not be is inert. You end a Mars year knowing more about your own force, because you spent twelve months being asked to use it.

Astrologers who use annual profections say every year of your life has a planetary lord, and yours right now is Jupiter, the planet the tradition counts as the most helpful of the seven. A Jupiter administration governs by opening doors. This tends to be a year where the world says yes more often: opportunities arrive, useful people appear, and problems that needed a stroke of luck get one. Growth is the theme, and it takes whatever form your life has room for. Study and travel sit high on Jupiter's list, along with teachers, mentors, publishing, and anything that widens what you know or how far you can see. Questions of meaning come with the territory, since Jupiter concerns belief: what you have faith in, what you think life is for, where you are willing to hope. Generosity flows both ways in a Jupiter year; you receive more, and you have more worth giving. The classic caution is excess. Jupiter enlarges whatever it touches, including commitments, appetites, and optimism, so the year's stumbles usually come from taking on too much rather than too little. Promises made in a season of confidence still come due later. The place to watch is your natal Jupiter. Its condition sets the size of the door this year can open, and transits to it time the openings themselves: the offer, the acceptance, the introduction that changes your reach. Jupiter in the moving sky changes sign about once a year too, and during its own year that shift lands close to home. Growth is quiet while it happens. A Jupiter year often looks ordinary from inside and large in hindsight, once you notice how much more room you have than you did on the birthday that opened it.

Profections, the birthday-count technique astrologers use to time the years, put Saturn in charge of this one for you. Saturn is the manager who takes the job seriously. A year under it moves at a deliberate pace and keeps strict books: effort is recorded, shortcuts are noticed, and rewards arrive late but keep. The themes are structure and weight. Responsibilities grow, sometimes because you seek them and sometimes because they find you, and the year asks whether your commitments are ones you actually mean. Whatever in your life has been running on habit or luck gets tested for load-bearing strength. Some structures pass and become permanent. Some fail, and the failure, though rarely pleasant, tells the truth. Time itself becomes a felt presence: deadlines, aging, endings, the long view. Discipline stops being a virtue you admire and becomes a tool you use. A Saturn year favors the work that compounds, the slow skill, the debt retired, the foundation poured, and it is famously unmoved by haste. Loneliness can shade the year at moments, since Saturn separates in order to clarify; solitude you choose feels very different from solitude you drift into, and you have some say in which one you get. Follow the year through your own Saturn. Its natal condition tells you how this manager treats you in particular, and the transits reaching it this year mark the exams: the weeks when the year's structures are stress-tested and its real gains locked in. Saturn years have a reputation for being hard, and many are genuinely demanding. They are also the years people point to afterward and say: that is when it got solid. You tend to leave carrying less than you brought in and owning more than you started with, because what remains is the part that holds.
